causes.label: Resolver of motor B delivering unequal or distorted sine/cosine signals
High contact resistance or moisture in the resolver connector
Fault inside the rear motor assembly incl. bearing damage (Mitsubishi)
Damaged shielding letting inverter noise into the resolver lines

symptoms: Hybrid system warning and MIL
Rear or second motor disabled, reduced traction or power
Jerky torque delivery before the fault sets

P0A47.title: Drive Motor B Position Sensor Circuit Low
P0A47.description: P0A47 means a resolver signal of motor B is below its allowed range, typically from a sine, cosine or excitation line shorted to ground or a shorted coil. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. Mitsubishi files low resolver signals of the 2023 Outlander PHEV rear motor under its own codes instead: P0C57 for sine and P0C61 for cosine at 0.3 V or less for 0.18 s. Kia uses the motor A twin P0A41 on the Optima Hybrid and blames shorts or pin fit in the sub-harness. CARB 1968.2 requires circuit monitoring of electric drive components, and Bosch patents show how a ground short is told apart by line offset. P0A48 is the high side, P0A45 the general circuit fault. Expect a warning lamp and reduced motor B drive.

causes.label: Resolver sine, cosine or excitation line shorted to ground
Poor pin fit or water ingress at the motor B resolver connector
Shorted resolver coil inside motor B
Faulty resolver input stage in the motor control module

symptoms: MIL or hybrid service lamp
Second motor disabled, reduced traction or power
Fault may come and go with vibration or moisture

P0A48.title: Drive Motor B Position Sensor Circuit High
P0A48.description: P0A48 reports a motor B resolver line reading above its allowed range, for example a sine, cosine or excitation wire shorted to a supply voltage, or an open coil whose line is pulled up by the input bias circuit until the converter clips. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. Mitsubishi handles high resolver voltages on the 2023 Outlander PHEV with its own codes (P0C53/P0C5D at 4.9 V or more on the front motor, P0C58/P0C62 on the rear), and Kia uses the motor A twin P0A42 on the Optima Hybrid. CARB 1968.2 requires circuit checks of electric drive components; Bosch patents describe detecting an open sine or cosine line and a short to supply. P0A47 is the low side. Expect a warning lamp and loss of motor B.

causes.label: Resolver line shorted to a supply voltage
Open sine or cosine line pulled high by the input circuit
Corroded or loose terminals at the motor B resolver connector
Faulty resolver input stage in the motor control module

symptoms: MIL and hybrid system warning
Second motor disabled, reduced traction or power
Vehicle may not enter ready mode

P0A49.title: Drive Motor B Position Sensor Circuit Intermittent
P0A49.description: P0A49 covers short dropouts or jumps in the motor B resolver signal that are too brief to count as a lasting loss, low or high fault. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. The motor A twin P0A43 is used by Stellantis on the Pacifica Hybrid, where dealers must check bulletins and reflash the hybrid control processor before replacing the power inverter module. GM shows on the Bolt that a slightly spread resolver terminal can cause brief signal loss and a sudden loss of drive, and forbids splicing resolver connectors because the circuits are sensitive. CARB 1968.2 requires detection of intermittent circuit faults of drive components. P0A45 is the permanent fault. Expect a warning that may clear after a restart.

causes.label: Loose or spread terminal in the motor B resolver connector
Chafed or stretched resolver wiring near the rear axle or subframe
Moisture in the connector causing intermittent leakage
Hybrid control software needing an update

symptoms: Hybrid warning or MIL that comes and goes
Brief loss of second-motor drive, often over bumps
Code stored as history without current symptoms

P0A4A.title: Drive Motor B Position Sensor Circuit Overspeed
P0A4A.description: P0A4A reports that the speed calculated from the motor B resolver exceeds the motor's permitted maximum. Mitsubishi uses it for the rear motor of the 2023 Outlander PHEV: set at 12,500 rpm or more for at least 1 s with supply above 8 V, and only judged once the rear position sensor codes P0A45, P0A46, P0C57, P0C58, P0C61 and P0C62 are ruled out; otherwise the rear motor assembly is replaced, bearing damage being one listed cause. GM uses its own code P1B0E (above 11,500 rpm, Type A) for this check on the second motor of its two-mode trucks. CARB 1968.2 requires monitoring of electric drive components. P0A44 is the motor A twin. Expect the rear motor to be shut off to protect it, with less traction.

causes.label: Fault in the rear motor assembly, e.g. damaged bearing or control unit (Mitsubishi)
Real overspeed from rear wheel spin on low grip
Disturbed resolver signal producing a false speed value

symptoms: Rear electric drive shut off, front-wheel drive only
Hybrid/EV warning and MIL
Reduced acceleration in limp mode

P0A4B.title: Generator Position Sensor Circuit
P0A4B.description: P0A4B covers the resolver that tells the inverter where the generator rotor stands; without a valid angle the generator cannot be commutated. Mitsubishi (Outlander PHEV 2023) runs the check continuously once the generator control unit has at least 8.0 V and sets P0A4B when its internal status flags stay failed for 0.23 s or 0.28 s; low and high signal levels go to separate codes there. Volvo lists P0A4B in the inverter generator module of its 2022-23 plug-in hybrids, as permanent or intermittent fault, with no-start complaints, and fixed false detections by software only. P0A4C is the plausibility check, P0A4D/P0A4E the low and high signal, P0A4F a sporadic signal, P0A50 overspeed. The driver sees a hybrid warning and may lose electric drive or engine start.

causes.label: False detection in the inverter monitor software (Volvo, fixed by update)
Damaged resolver wiring or connector between generator and inverter
Generator resolver defective
Resolver evaluation in the power drive unit faulty

symptoms: Hybrid system warning and MIL
Engine does not start or crank in hybrid mode
Electric drive or charging by the generator disabled

P0A4C.title: Generator Position Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
P0A4C.description: P0A4C means the generator resolver delivers signals that are electrically present but implausible, so the computed rotor angle cannot be trusted. Mitsubishi documents the exact limits for the 2023 Outlander PHEV: the sine or cosine winding voltage must stay between 2.1 and 2.9 V; if either leaves that window for 0.28 s, or an internal status fault persists for 0.31 s, the generator control unit stores P0A4C. Typical triggers are a corroded or loose resolver plug, a chafed shield picking up noise, a winding that has drifted, or a faulty input stage in the power drive unit. P0A4B is the general circuit fault, P0A4D and P0A4E the hard low and high signal, P0A4F a sporadic dropout. Expect a hybrid warning, reduced power and possibly no engine start via the generator.

causes.label: Corroded or loose resolver connector
Damaged shielding letting interference onto the sine/cosine lines
Resolver winding drifted out of tolerance
Faulty resolver input stage in the power drive unit

symptoms: Hybrid system warning and MIL
Reduced drive power or engine-only operation
Engine start via the generator not possible

P0A4D.title: Generator Position Sensor Circuit Low
P0A4D.description: P0A4D reports a generator resolver signal stuck below its permitted range, as caused by a sine, cosine or excitation line shorted to ground or a winding short. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. Mitsubishi shows how the fault is judged but files it under its own codes: on the 2023 Outlander PHEV a sine or cosine voltage at or below 2.0 V for 0.21 s sets P0C66 or P0C6B instead of P0A4D. A Bosch patent describes distinguishing a short to ground from a short to supply by the offset of the receiver coil lines, which is the basis for low/high splitting. CARB requires such circuit checks for hybrid input components. P0A4E is the high side, P0A4B the general circuit fault, P0A4C plausibility. The hybrid system typically shuts the generator down and warns the driver.

causes.label: Sine, cosine or excitation line shorted to ground
Moisture or corrosion in the resolver connector
Shorted resolver winding inside the generator

symptoms: Hybrid system warning and MIL
Generator disabled, engine-only or no-start condition

P0A4E.title: Generator Position Sensor Circuit High
P0A4E.description: P0A4E is set when a generator resolver signal sits above its permitted range, which usually points to an open signal line pulled up by the input circuit or a short to a supply voltage. No manufacturer documents P0A4E publicly. Mitsubishi evaluates the same condition on the 2023 Outlander PHEV but reports it under its own codes: a sine or cosine voltage of 4.9 V or more for 0.21 s stores P0C67 or P0C6C. A Bosch patent explains how the averaged offset of the receiver coil lines reveals whether a line is shorted to supply rather than to ground. CARB requires out-of-range checks for hybrid input components. P0A4D is the low counterpart, P0A4B the general circuit code, P0A4C the plausibility check. The generator is usually shut off and the hybrid warning comes on.

causes.label: Open resolver signal line or pushed-out terminal
Signal line shorted to a supply voltage
Faulty resolver input stage in the power drive unit

symptoms: Hybrid system warning and MIL
Generator disabled, engine-only or no-start condition

P0A4F.title: Generator Position Sensor Circuit Intermittent
P0A4F.description: P0A4F flags a generator resolver signal that drops out or jumps briefly and then recovers, as opposed to a steady fault. No manufacturer documents P0A4F publicly. Mitsubishi and Volvo handle short interruptions inside the general circuit code instead: Volvo lists P0A4B in its inverter generator module with the fault type intermittent, and Mitsubishi tells technicians to treat a resolver fault that cannot be reproduced as an intermittent malfunction of harness and connectors. CARB requires circuit continuity checks on hybrid input components. Loose terminals, fretting contacts, a chafed cable near moving parts or heat-related cracks are the usual suspects. P0A4B is the steady circuit fault, P0A4C plausibility, P0A4D/P0A4E low and high. Symptoms come and go, often with a brief loss of hybrid function.

causes.label: Loose or fretting terminals in the resolver connectors
Chafed resolver cable that breaks contact under vibration
Heat-related cracks in wiring or solder joints

symptoms: Hybrid warning that appears and clears again
Short loss of electric drive or jerky power delivery
Fault often linked to bumps or heat

P0A50.title: Generator Position Sensor Circuit Overspeed
P0A50.description: P0A50 says the generator speed derived from its resolver has exceeded the permitted maximum. Mitsubishi documents it for the 2023 Outlander PHEV: with at least 8.0 V at the generator control unit and the position sensor itself judged healthy, a speed of 15,500 rpm or more lasting 0.5 s stores P0A50, and the repair path ends with replacing the generator. Because a resolver fault would already be caught by P0A4B to P0A4F, an overspeed entry usually reflects a real mechanical overspeed, for example from a transaxle or clutch problem, or an internal generator fault. The drive motor counterparts are P0A44 and P0A4A. CARB requires hybrid components to be monitored. Expect a hybrid warning and the generator being shut off to protect it.

causes.label: Internal generator fault (Mitsubishi repair path ends with generator replacement)
Mechanical fault in the transaxle or clutch letting the generator overrun
Incorrect speed calculation in the power drive unit

symptoms: Hybrid system warning and MIL
Generator shut off, reduced power or engine-only drive

P0A51.title: Drive Motor A Current Sensor Circuit
P0A51.description: P0A51 reports a fault in the circuit of the current sensor that measures the phase current of drive motor A. The inverter needs this value for torque control and overcurrent protection. No manufacturer documents P0A51 publicly with its criteria. A Toyota patent shows the principle: a control sensor and a monitoring sensor measure the same motor current, and if the control sensor sits in its ground-short range or the two differ beyond a threshold over several cycles, the system flags the sensor and opens the main relays, because a wrong reading could drive the inverter into overcurrent. CARB requires circuit checks of hybrid input components. P0A52 covers plausibility, P0A53/P0A54 low and high; P0A55 is motor B. The hybrid system usually shuts down drive motor A.

causes.label: Current sensor in the inverter assembly failed
Sensor supply or signal line interrupted inside the inverter
Evaluation circuit on the motor control board faulty

symptoms: Hybrid system warning and MIL
Drive motor A disabled, vehicle may not move or runs on engine only

P0A52.title: Drive Motor A Current Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
P0A52.description: P0A52 means the current sensor of drive motor A delivers values that are electrically valid but do not fit the operating state. Typical checks compare the reading at zero current with its expected offset, or compare redundant sensors with each other. No manufacturer documents P0A52 publicly. A Hyundai patent describes compensating the sensor offset while no current flows and declaring the compensation abnormal when the offset leaves its allowed band; a Toyota patent compares a control sensor with a monitoring sensor and flags a lasting difference. CARB requires rationality checks of hybrid input components. P0A51 is the general circuit fault, P0A53 and P0A54 the hard low and high signal. A wrong current reading can cause torque errors, so the system limits or disables drive motor A.

causes.label: Sensor offset drifted beyond the compensation range
Control and monitoring sensor disagree due to one degraded sensor
Electrical interference or poor ground on the sensor signal

symptoms: Hybrid system warning and MIL
Reduced or jerky electric drive
Drive motor A disabled, engine-only operation

P0A53.title: Drive Motor A Current Sensor Circuit Low
P0A53.description: P0A53 is stored when the current sensor signal of drive motor A stays below its valid range, typically from a signal line shorted to ground, a lost sensor supply or a failed Hall element. No manufacturer documents P0A53 publicly. A Toyota patent explains why this matters: a sensor stuck in its ground-short range reports far less current than actually flows, so the current controller keeps raising the drive and can push the inverter into overcurrent; the described system therefore turns off the system relay and warns the driver once the condition repeats over consecutive cycles. CARB requires out-of-range checks for hybrid input components. P0A54 is the high counterpart, P0A51 the general circuit code, P0A52 plausibility. Drive motor A is shut down.

causes.label: Sensor signal line shorted to ground
Sensor supply voltage missing
Hall element of the current sensor failed

symptoms: Hybrid system warning and MIL
High-voltage system switched off, vehicle may not move

P0A54.title: Drive Motor A Current Sensor Circuit High
P0A54.description: P0A54 signals that the current sensor output of drive motor A sits above its valid range, as caused by an open ground, a short to the sensor supply or an internal sensor fault that saturates the output. No manufacturer documents P0A54 publicly. Patents from Toyota and Hyundai show how inverter controllers judge current sensors: by checking the reading against fixed electrical limits, by comparing a control and a monitoring sensor, and by verifying the offset while no current flows. A reading pinned high would make the controller cut drive torque or trigger overcurrent protection without reason. CARB requires out-of-range checks for hybrid input components. P0A53 is the low side, P0A51 the general circuit fault, P0A52 plausibility, P0A58 the same check on motor B.

causes.label: Open ground of the current sensor
Signal line shorted to the sensor supply
Internal sensor fault with saturated output

symptoms: Hybrid system warning and MIL
Drive motor A disabled or power strongly reduced

P0A55.title: Drive Motor B Current Sensor Circuit
P0A55.description: P0A55 is the general circuit fault of the current sensor that measures the current of drive motor B, typically the second traction motor, for example on a rear axle. The inverter needs this signal for torque control and to protect its power switches. No manufacturer documents P0A55 publicly. A Toyota patent shows the principle behind such checks: a control sensor and a monitoring sensor watch the same motor current, and a sensor stuck in its ground-short range or a lasting gap between the two leads to the relays opening. CARB requires circuit checks of hybrid input components. P0A56 is plausibility, P0A57/P0A58 low and high; P0A51 is the same fault on motor A. Usually drive motor B is switched off and the car drives on reduced power.

causes.label: Current sensor of drive motor B failed (usually inside the inverter)
Sensor supply or signal line interrupted or shorted
Evaluation circuit on the motor B control board faulty

symptoms: Hybrid or electric drive warning with MIL
Drive motor B disabled, loss of electric all-wheel drive or reduced power

P0A56.title: Drive Motor B Current Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
P0A56.description: P0A56 means the current sensor of drive motor B delivers electrically valid values that do not match the operating state, for example a zero-current offset outside its band or a reading that disagrees with a redundant sensor. No manufacturer documents P0A56 publicly. A Hyundai patent covering both the traction motor and the starter-generator flags an abnormal offset compensation by comparing an estimated power-module temperature with the measured inverter temperature; a Caterpillar patent checks that the phase currents of a motor add up to roughly zero. CARB requires rationality checks of hybrid input components. P0A55 is the general circuit fault, P0A57/P0A58 the hard low and high signal, P0A52 the motor A counterpart. Motor B is limited or switched off.

causes.label: Current sensor offset drifted or offset learning disturbed
Current sensor of drive motor B degraded
Electrical interference on the sensor signal

symptoms: Hybrid warning and MIL
Reduced or missing drive from motor B

P0A57.title: Drive Motor B Current Sensor Circuit Low
P0A57.description: P0A57 is set when the signal of the drive motor B current sensor stays below its valid range, usually from a signal line shorted to ground, a missing sensor supply or a failed Hall element. No manufacturer documents P0A57 publicly. A Toyota patent explains the risk of this failure: a sensor held in its ground-short range reports much less current than really flows, the current controller raises its output and can drive the inverter into overcurrent; the system described therefore opens the system relays and warns the driver once the condition repeats. CARB requires out-of-range checks for hybrid input components. P0A58 is the high side, P0A55 the general circuit code, P0A56 plausibility, P0A53 the same check on motor A. Motor B is shut down.

causes.label: Sensor signal line shorted to ground
Sensor supply voltage missing
Hall element of the current sensor failed

symptoms: Hybrid warning and MIL
Drive motor B or the whole high-voltage system switched off

P0A58.title: Drive Motor B Current Sensor Circuit High
P0A58.description: P0A58 reports that the output of the drive motor B current sensor sits above its valid range, for instance from an open sensor ground, a short to the sensor supply or an internal fault that saturates the output. No manufacturer documents P0A58 publicly. Patents from Toyota and Hyundai show how motor controllers judge their current sensors: against fixed electrical limits, by comparing a control with a monitoring sensor, and by checking the zero-current offset. A reading pinned high would make the controller withdraw torque or trip overcurrent protection although nothing is wrong in the motor. CARB requires out-of-range checks for hybrid input components. P0A57 is the low side, P0A55 the general circuit fault, P0A56 plausibility, P0A54 the motor A equivalent.

causes.label: Sensor ground open or high resistance
Signal line shorted to the sensor supply
Current sensor with saturated output

symptoms: Hybrid warning and MIL
Drive motor B disabled, reduced power

P0A59.title: Generator Current Sensor Circuit
P0A59.description: P0A59 is the general circuit fault of the current sensor on the hybrid generator, the electric machine driven by the engine that charges the battery and often starts the engine. Its inverter uses the current reading to control generator torque. No manufacturer documents P0A59 publicly with criteria. Patents describe the same sensing on generators: Toyota for a motor that also works as an engine-driven generator, Hyundai for the hybrid starter-generator, where two phases are measured and the third is calculated, and Caterpillar for generator and traction motor sensors. CARB requires circuit checks of hybrid input components. P0A5A is plausibility, P0A5B/P0A5C low and high. Without a valid reading the generator is disabled, so charging and engine start can be affected.

causes.label: Generator current sensor failed (usually inside the inverter)
Sensor supply or signal line interrupted or shorted
Evaluation circuit on the generator control board faulty

symptoms: Hybrid warning and MIL
Engine runs constantly or the high-voltage battery is no longer charged
Vehicle may not enter ready mode

P0A5A.title: Generator Current Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
P0A5A.description: P0A5A means the generator current sensor delivers values that are electrically valid but implausible, for example a wrong zero offset or phase currents that no longer add up. No hybrid manufacturer documents P0A5A publicly with criteria. A Hyundai patent for a motor and hybrid starter-generator system measures two phase currents, derives the third from the zero-sum rule and detects a faulty offset compensation by comparing estimated power-module temperature with measured inverter temperature. A Caterpillar patent flags sensors on generator and traction motor when the phase currents do not sum to near zero. CARB requires rationality checks of hybrid input components. P0A59 is the circuit fault, P0A5B/P0A5C the hard low and high signal. The generator is limited or switched off.

causes.label: Generator current sensor offset drifted or offset learning disturbed
Generator current sensor degraded
Control module calibration requiring an update

symptoms: Hybrid warning and MIL
Reduced charging or engine running more often

P0A5B.title: Generator Current Sensor Circuit Low
P0A5B.description: P0A5B indicates that the signal of the generator current sensor stays below its valid range, as caused by a signal line shorted to ground, a lost sensor supply or a failed sensing element. No hybrid manufacturer documents P0A5B publicly with criteria. A Toyota patent covering a motor that also serves as an engine-driven generator shows why the low side is critical: a sensor held in its ground-short range under-reports the real current, the controller keeps increasing the drive, and overcurrent becomes possible, so the system opens its relays after repeated detection. CARB requires out-of-range checks for hybrid input components. P0A5C is the high side, P0A59 the circuit fault, P0A5A plausibility, P0A57 the motor B equivalent. Generator operation stops.

causes.label: Sensor signal line shorted to ground
Sensor supply voltage missing
Sensing element of the generator current sensor failed

symptoms: Hybrid warning and MIL
High-voltage system switched off or battery no longer charged

P0A5C.title: Generator Current Sensor Circuit High
P0A5C.description: P0A5C means the generator current sensor output lies above its valid range, typically from an open sensor ground, a short to the sensor supply or a saturated sensor. No hybrid manufacturer documents P0A5C publicly with criteria. Patents describe how controllers of engine-driven generators and starter-generators supervise their current sensors: Toyota with a control and a monitoring sensor plus fixed signal limits, Hyundai with an offset check on the two measured phases from which the third is calculated. A falsely high reading makes the controller reduce generator torque or trip overcurrent protection. CARB requires out-of-range checks for hybrid input components. P0A5B is the low side, P0A59 the circuit fault, P0A5A plausibility, P0A58 the motor B counterpart.

causes.label: Sensor ground open or high resistance
Signal line shorted to the sensor supply
Generator current sensor with saturated output

symptoms: Hybrid warning and MIL
Generator disabled, engine start or battery charging affected

P0A5D.title: Drive Motor A Phase U Current
P0A5D.description: P0A5D concerns the current in phase U of drive motor A, as seen by the inverter. Audi documents it on the 2021-23 Q5 e quattro (bulletin 2069917/1): P0A5D00, often with P0A6000 and P0A6300, is stored in the electric drive control module J841, the cluster reads Drive system: fault and the car may not start or drive. The cause was variance in welding the high-voltage phase conductors; the fix is a resistance and wiggle test of each phase lead and a new motor harness. Many inverters do not measure U at all: a Hyundai patent measures two phases and calculates the third from the zero-sum rule, so a U fault can also stem from the V or W sensor. P0A5E/P0A5F are the low and high variants, P0A60 and P0A63 phases V and W.

causes.label: High-voltage phase cable or weld joint to drive motor A faulty (Audi Q5 e quattro)
Phase current sensor in the inverter failed
Internal inverter fault
Winding fault in phase U of drive motor A

symptoms: Drive system fault message and MIL
Vehicle does not start or the drive system cannot be activated

P0A5E.title: Drive Motor A Phase U Current Low
P0A5E.description: P0A5E means too little current flows, or is sensed, in phase U of drive motor A, the classic sign of an open phase. GM describes the check for the motor control processor of the 2016 Chevrolet Volt and in its 2018 hybrid tables: with the inverter in normal PWM above 50 V and a squared current command above 900 A2 (2016) or 4,900 A2 (2018), the absolute U current is sampled while the rotor is within 30 degrees of the U phase axis; below 9 A for 0.4 s of a 0.6 s window, P0A5E sets as Type A, MIL on the first trip. Each phase is tested in turn as the rotor turns. A Caterpillar patent likewise spots a dead sensor by a phase reading near zero. P0A61 and P0A64 are phases V and W, P0A5F the high side, P0A5D the general U code.

causes.label: Open circuit in the phase U cable, connector or terminal
Phase U current sensor reads zero
Phase U switch of the inverter not conducting
Open winding of phase U in drive motor A

symptoms: MIL and propulsion system warning
Rough or reduced electric drive, possible engine-only operation

P0A5F.title: Drive Motor A Phase U Current High
P0A5F.description: P0A5F reports excessive current in phase U of drive motor A, a condition the inverter treats as overcurrent. Hyundai documents it on the 2017 Ioniq Hybrid (bulletin 17-01-057-1, campaign T2J): coolant leaking inside the traction motor set the Check Engine and hybrid lights with P0A5F, P0A62 or P0A65, often together with the isolation fault P0AA6; drivers noticed weak acceleration and a dead air conditioner. The procedure runs an insulation breakdown test with the scan tool and replaces the motor if it fails. A Hyundai patent shows such inverters measure two phases and calculate the third. P0A5E is the low side, P0A5D the general U code, P0A62 and P0A65 the same overcurrent on V and W.

causes.label: Internal coolant leak in the traction motor causing insulation breakdown (Hyundai Ioniq Hybrid)
Shorted winding or phase lead of drive motor A
Inverter power stage fault in phase U
Current sensor falsely reporting overcurrent

symptoms: Check Engine and hybrid warning lights
Reduced power when accelerating
Air conditioning inoperative (Hyundai Ioniq Hybrid)

P0A60.title: Drive Motor A Phase V Current
P0A60.description: P0A60 covers the current in phase V of drive motor A. Toyota uses it with sub codes: a field report filed with NHTSA describes a 2006 Highlander Hybrid whose master warning lit and which would not move; P0A60 sub code 501 had set first, followed by P0A63, P0A78 and P0AEF, all returning at once after clearing, and the inverter assembly was replaced. Another Highlander showed P0A60 and P0A63 together with the generator phase codes P0A72 and P0A75, again an inverter fault; Toyota lists only V and W phases there, matching inverters that measure two phases and calculate the third. Audi stores P0A6000 on the 2021-23 Q5 e quattro for a faulty high-voltage phase lead. P0A61/P0A62 are low and high, P0A5D and P0A63 phases U and W.

causes.label: Internal fault in the inverter assembly (Toyota Highlander Hybrid)
High-voltage phase V cable or weld joint faulty (Audi Q5 e quattro)
Phase V current sensor failed
Winding fault in phase V of drive motor A

symptoms: Master warning or drive system fault message, MIL
Vehicle will not move or start

P0A61.title: Drive Motor A Phase V Current Low
P0A61.description: P0A61 indicates that phase V of drive motor A carries, or reports, too little current when it should be near its peak, pointing to an open phase V circuit. GM uses the same peak-axis test as for phase U on the 2016 Chevrolet Volt motor control processor and in its 2018 hybrid tables, here with the rotor within 30 degrees of the V phase axis: inverter above 50 V in normal PWM, squared current command above 900 A2 in 2016 and 4,900 A2 from 2018, a peak phase current under 9 A for 0.4 s within 0.6 s, Type A with MIL on the first trip. On inverters that sense only two phases a dead V sensor also corrupts the calculated third phase. A Caterpillar patent detects such a sensor by a near-zero phase reading. P0A62 is the high side, P0A5E and P0A64 cover U and W.

causes.label: Open circuit in the phase V cable, connector or terminal
Phase V current sensor reads zero
Phase V switch of the inverter not conducting
Open winding of phase V in drive motor A

symptoms: MIL and propulsion system warning
Jerky or weak electric drive

P0A62.title: Drive Motor A Phase V Current High
P0A62.description: P0A62 signals overcurrent in phase V of drive motor A. Hyundai lists it in bulletin 17-01-057-1 for the 2017 Ioniq Hybrid next to P0A5F, P0A65 and the isolation fault P0AA6: the bulletin traces them to coolant leaking inside the traction motor and checks the high-voltage insulation first. Check Engine and hybrid lights came on, acceleration weakened and the air conditioning stopped. The dealer first runs an isolation breakdown test with the scan tool, then checks the motor for coolant and replaces it if needed. A shorted turn or a damaged phase lead to ground gives the same picture on other vehicles. A Hyundai patent describes two measured phases with the third calculated. P0A61 is the low side, P0A60 the general V code, P0A5F and P0A65 phases U and W.

causes.label: Coolant inside the traction motor with loss of insulation (Hyundai Ioniq Hybrid)
Phase V lead or winding shorted to ground or to another phase
Inverter power stage fault in phase V

symptoms: Check Engine and hybrid warning lights
Weak acceleration, air conditioning inoperative

P0A63.title: Drive Motor A Phase W Current
P0A63.description: P0A63 concerns the current in phase W of drive motor A. In the Toyota field reports filed with NHTSA it always appears beside P0A60: on a 2006 Highlander Hybrid with sub code 502, after P0A60 sub code 501, together with P0A78 and P0AEF, master warning on and no drive; the inverter assembly was replaced. These Toyota reports name only V and W, for the motor and for the generator (P0A72, P0A75), which fits a design where two phase currents are measured and U follows from the rule that all three add up to zero, as a Hyundai patent describes. Audi stores P0A6300 in module J841 of the 2021-23 Q5 e quattro when the welded high-voltage phase lead fails. P0A64/P0A65 are low and high, P0A5D and P0A60 phases U and V.

causes.label: Internal fault in the inverter assembly (Toyota Highlander Hybrid)
High-voltage phase W cable or weld joint faulty (Audi Q5 e quattro)
Phase W current sensor failed

symptoms: Master warning or drive system fault message, MIL
Vehicle will not move or start

P0A64.title: Drive Motor A Phase W Current Low
P0A64.description: P0A64 means phase W of drive motor A shows too little current at the moment it should peak, typically an open W lead or a W sensor stuck at zero. GM completes its three-phase sequence with this code on the 2016 Chevrolet Volt motor control processor and in the 2018 hybrid tables: when the rotor sits within 30 degrees of the W phase axis, the inverter runs normal PWM above 50 V and the squared current command exceeds 900 A2 (2016) or 4,900 A2 (2018), a W peak below 9 A for 0.4 s of a 0.6 s window sets P0A64 as Type A, MIL on the first trip. Because the rotor passes each axis in turn, only the open phase is flagged. A Caterpillar patent uses a near-zero phase reading the same way. P0A65 is the high side, P0A5E and P0A61 cover U and V.

causes.label: Open circuit in the phase W cable, connector or terminal
Phase W current sensor reads zero
Phase W switch of the inverter not conducting
Open winding of phase W in drive motor A

symptoms: MIL and propulsion system warning
Uneven or reduced electric drive torque

P0A65.title: Drive Motor A Phase W Current High
P0A65.description: P0A65 reports overcurrent in phase W of drive motor A. It is the third phase code in Hyundai bulletin 17-01-057-1 for the 2017 Ioniq Hybrid, campaign T2J: with an internal coolant leak in the traction motor, P0A65, P0A5F or P0A62 set with Check Engine and hybrid lights, often joined by the isolation fault P0AA6. Reduced power when accelerating and a non-working air conditioner followed. The fix path is the scan tool isolation test, a coolant inspection of the motor and, if confirmed, a new traction motor. In general, a W-phase winding short or a pinched cable has the same effect. Hyundai inverters measure two phases and calculate the third, per a Hyundai patent. P0A64 is the low side, P0A63 the general W code, P0A5F and P0A62 phases U and V.

causes.label: Internal coolant leak in the traction motor (Hyundai Ioniq Hybrid)
Phase W lead or winding shorted to ground or to another phase
Inverter power stage fault in phase W
Current sensor falsely reporting overcurrent

symptoms: Check Engine and hybrid warning lights
Reduced power when accelerating
Air conditioning inoperative (Hyundai Ioniq Hybrid)

P0A66.title: Drive Motor B Phase U Current
P0A66.description: P0A66 is the general fault code for the current in phase U of drive motor B, the second electric machine of a two-motor hybrid or an electric rear-axle motor. No manufacturer documents P0A66 publicly; GM, for instance, only uses the open-phase code P0A67 for this phase. The checks behind such a code are described in patents: a Caterpillar patent declares a phase sensor failed when the three phase currents no longer add up to roughly zero, and a Hyundai patent shows inverters that measure two phases and calculate the third. CARB requires circuit and rationality monitoring of electric drive components. P0A67 and P0A68 are the low and high variants, P0A69 and P0A6C cover phases V and W, P0A5D is the same code on motor A. Motor B is normally shut off.

causes.label: Phase U current sensor of motor B failed (inside the inverter)
Phase U high-voltage cable or terminal between inverter and motor B faulty
Internal fault in the motor B power stage
Winding fault in phase U of drive motor B

symptoms: Hybrid system warning and MIL
Motor B switched off, less power or no electric all-wheel drive

P0A67.title: Drive Motor B Phase U Current Low
P0A67.description: P0A67 reports that phase U of drive motor B carries too little current at the moment it should peak, which GM interprets as an open circuit in that phase. In the 2016 Chevrolet Volt tables for motor control processor B the test runs while the rotor is within 30 degrees of the U axis, the inverter is above 50 V in normal PWM and the squared current command exceeds 900 A²; a peak below 9 A for 0.4 s within a 0.6 s window sets a Type A fault with MIL on the first trip. GM's 2018 tables shared by the Volt and the CT6 plug-in keep the test but raise the command threshold to 4,900 A². P0A68 is the high side, P0A6A and P0A6D are phases V and W, P0A5E the motor A counterpart. Motor B is disabled.

causes.label: Open circuit in the phase U cable, connector or terminal of motor B
Phase U switch of the motor B inverter not conducting
Phase U current sensor stuck at zero
Open winding of phase U in drive motor B

symptoms: MIL on the first trip and propulsion system warning
Jerky or weak electric drive, reduced power

P0A68.title: Drive Motor B Phase U Current High
P0A68.description: P0A68 means the current measured in phase U of drive motor B rises above its plausible maximum, either because a real overcurrent flows, for example through damaged insulation, a winding short or a shorted power switch, or because the phase sensor reads too high. No manufacturer documents P0A68 publicly. For the motor A counterpart P0A5F, Hyundai links phase-high codes on the 2017 Ioniq Hybrid to coolant leaking inside the traction motor, together with an insulation fault. A Toyota patent explains why the inverter must react quickly: overcurrent loads the power switches and can destroy them, so the drive is cut. CARB requires monitoring of electric drive components. P0A67 is the low side, P0A6B and P0A6E cover V and W. Motor B is shut down.

causes.label: Winding short or insulation breakdown in phase U of motor B (e.g. coolant ingress)
Shorted power switch in the phase U leg of the inverter
Phase U current sensor reading too high (gain or offset fault)

symptoms: Hybrid warning and MIL, often with an insulation fault code
Sudden loss of drive from motor B

P0A69.title: Drive Motor B Phase V Current
P0A69.description: P0A69 flags a general fault in the current of phase V of drive motor B. No manufacturer documents P0A69 publicly. Phase V matters doubly on many inverters: a Hyundai patent describes designs that measure only two of the three phase currents and calculate the remaining one, so a faulty V reading also distorts the computed phase. A Caterpillar patent detects a failed sensor through the zero-sum rule of the three phase currents and can then estimate the missing value. CARB requires monitoring of electric drive components for circuit faults and plausibility. P0A6A and P0A6B are the low and high variants, P0A66 and P0A6C phases U and W, P0A60 the motor A equivalent. The driver sees a hybrid warning and motor B is taken out of service.

causes.label: Phase V current sensor of motor B failed
Fault on the motor B inverter board or power stage
Phase V high-voltage cable or terminal loose or damaged

symptoms: Hybrid system warning and MIL
Reduced power, motor B no longer contributes

P0A6A.title: Drive Motor B Phase V Current Low
P0A6A.description: P0A6A is GM's open-circuit test for phase V of drive motor B. The controller checks each phase on its own as the rotor turns; for phase V it looks at the window of 30 degrees either side of the V axis, where the current should be largest. With the inverter above 50 V in normal PWM and a squared current command above 900 A² (2016 Volt) or 4,900 A² (2018 and 2019 tables), a peak below 9 A for 0.4 s out of 0.6 s is a Type A failure with MIL after one trip. The 2016 Volt table describes this motor B code with the words drive motor A, an evident copy slip. A missing V current points to a broken lead, a dead switch or a sensor stuck at zero. P0A6B is the high side, P0A67 and P0A6D phases U and W, P0A61 the motor A code.

causes.label: Phase V lead, connector or bolted terminal of motor B open
Phase V switch of the motor B inverter not switching
Phase V current sensor output stuck at zero
Open phase V winding in motor B

symptoms: MIL and propulsion system warning after the first trip
Vibration or uneven torque from motor B before shutdown

P0A6B.title: Drive Motor B Phase V Current High
P0A6B.description: P0A6B is stored when phase V of drive motor B reports more current than the operating state allows. No manufacturer documents P0A6B publicly. Two causes must be told apart: a real overcurrent from a shorted switch, a winding fault or an insulation breakdown, and a sensor that reads high because its gain or zero offset has drifted. Patents show how inverters separate them: Toyota compares a control sensor against a monitoring sensor and the commanded current, Caterpillar checks that the three phase currents still sum to about zero. CARB requires plausibility monitoring of electric drive components. P0A6A is the low side, P0A68 and P0A6E the U and W phases, P0A62 the motor A counterpart. The inverter shuts motor B down to protect itself.

causes.label: Phase V current sensor gain or offset drifted high
Shorted power switch in the phase V leg
Winding or insulation fault in phase V of motor B

symptoms: Hybrid warning and MIL
Motor B cut out, reduced acceleration

P0A6C.title: Drive Motor B Phase W Current
P0A6C.description: P0A6C covers a general fault in the phase W current of drive motor B. No manufacturer documents P0A6C publicly. Where motor B sits on a separate axle, its three high-voltage phase leads are long and exposed, so cable and terminal faults are a realistic cause; for the motor A phase codes P0A5D, P0A60 and P0A63, Audi blames welding variances in the high-voltage wiring of the 2021-23 Q5 e quattro. On the sensing side, a Caterpillar patent recognises a dead phase sensor by its near-zero reading combined with a violated zero-sum of the three currents. CARB requires circuit and plausibility checks of drive components. P0A6D and P0A6E are the low and high cases, P0A66 and P0A69 phases U and V, P0A63 motor A. Motor B is switched off.

causes.label: Phase W high-voltage lead or terminal to motor B damaged or loose
Phase W current sensor failed
Internal fault of the motor B inverter

symptoms: Hybrid warning lamp and MIL
Loss of electric drive on the axle driven by motor B

P0A6D.title: Drive Motor B Phase W Current Low
P0A6D.description: P0A6D completes GM's set of open-phase tests for drive motor B with phase W. Because each phase is only judged while the rotor sits within 30 degrees of its own axis, the code points to W alone rather than to the motor as a whole. GM's tables for the 2016 Volt require a running drive, more than 50 V on the inverter in normal PWM and a squared current command above 900 A²; the 2018 tables for Volt and CT6 use 4,900 A². If the W peak stays under 9 A for 0.4 s within 0.6 s, the Type A fault turns on the MIL after one trip. Typical findings are an interrupted W lead or terminal, a non-conducting switch or a sensor reading zero. P0A6E is the high side, P0A67 and P0A6A phases U and V, P0A64 the motor A test.

causes.label: Phase W lead or terminal of motor B interrupted
Phase W switch of the inverter not conducting
Phase W current sensor stuck at zero
Open phase W winding in motor B

symptoms: MIL on the first trip with propulsion warning
Rough or reduced electric drive

P0A6E.title: Drive Motor B Phase W Current High
P0A6E.description: P0A6E indicates excessive current, measured or real, in phase W of drive motor B. No manufacturer documents P0A6E publicly. On the motor A side, Hyundai's 2017 Ioniq Hybrid campaign shows the typical real-world pattern: coolant leaking inside the traction motor set phase-high codes for U, V and W alongside a high-voltage isolation fault, with motor replacement once the leak is confirmed. A Toyota patent describes the protective logic: if current runs far above the command, the inverter is at risk, so the system stops switching and opens the relays. CARB requires monitoring of electric drive components. P0A6D is the low side, P0A68 and P0A6B the U and V phases, P0A65 motor A. Drive from motor B is lost until repair.

causes.label: Insulation breakdown or winding short in phase W (moisture, coolant)
Shorted switch in the phase W leg of the inverter
Phase W current sensor reading too high

symptoms: MIL and hybrid warning, possibly with an isolation fault
Motor B no longer drives; possible air conditioning shutdown

P0A6F.title: Generator Phase U Current
P0A6F.description: P0A6F is the general fault code for the phase U current of the hybrid generator, the motor-generator that is mainly driven by the engine, starts it and charges the battery, such as Toyota's MG1 or Hyundai's hybrid starter-generator. No manufacturer documents P0A6F publicly; Toyota's published field reports show generator codes for phases V and W only. A Hyundai patent describes an inverter that senses two or three generator phase currents through its own sensors, separate from those of the drive motor. CARB requires monitoring of electric drive components. P0A70 and P0A71 are the low and high variants, P0A72 and P0A75 phases V and W, P0A59 the generator current sensor circuit. Without the generator, engine start and charging may fail.

causes.label: Generator phase U current sensor failed
Fault in the generator section of the inverter assembly
Generator phase U cable or terminal faulty

symptoms: Hybrid system warning and MIL
Engine cannot be started electrically or battery is no longer charged

P0A70.title: Generator Phase U Current Low
P0A70.description: P0A70 means phase U of the hybrid generator carries or reports too little current while the generator is loaded, typical of an open phase or a sensor stuck near zero. No manufacturer documents P0A70 publicly. The closest published test is GM's open-phase check for the drive motors (P0A67 and siblings), which compares the peak current near each phase axis against a 9 A threshold; GM publishes no such test for the generator. A Caterpillar patent identifies a failed phase sensor by a reading close to zero while the currents no longer sum to zero. CARB requires circuit monitoring of electric drive components. P0A71 is the high side, P0A73 and P0A76 phases V and W, P0A6F the general code. Engine start and charging can be affected.

causes.label: Open circuit in the generator phase U lead or terminal
Generator phase U current sensor stuck near zero
Phase U switch in the generator inverter not conducting

symptoms: Hybrid warning and MIL
Engine runs rough at start or battery charge level keeps dropping

P0A71.title: Generator Phase U Current High
P0A71.description: P0A71 is set when the current in phase U of the hybrid generator exceeds its permitted level. No manufacturer documents P0A71 publicly. The Toyota patent on current sensor monitoring applies directly, since its machine also runs as an engine-driven generator and starts the engine: a sensor stuck too low makes the controller push the real current far above command, and an overcurrent through the inverter can damage its switches, so the relays are opened. A real overcurrent can also come from a winding or insulation short in the generator or a shorted switch. CARB requires monitoring of electric drive components. P0A70 is the low side, P0A74 and P0A77 phases V and W, P0A6F the general code. The hybrid system usually shuts down.

causes.label: Shorted power switch in the generator phase U leg
Winding or insulation short in generator phase U
Faulty phase U current sensor or its evaluation in the inverter

symptoms: Master warning or hybrid warning with MIL
Hybrid system shuts down; vehicle may not move or restart

P0A72.title: Generator Phase V Current
P0A72.description: P0A72 reports a fault in the phase V current of the hybrid generator. Toyota uses it: a field report filed with NHTSA covers a 2006 Highlander Hybrid with the MIL on and P0A72 stored together with P0A75 for generator phase W, P0A60 and P0A63 for drive motor A, and inverter performance codes including P0A78; after checking connector fit and the resistance of the three-phase cables, the inverter/converter assembly was replaced. The pairing of V and W codes fits inverters that measure two phases and calculate the third, as a Hyundai patent describes for its starter-generator. P0A73 and P0A74 are the low and high cases, P0A6F and P0A75 phases U and W. Expect a hybrid warning and possibly no drive.

causes.label: Internal fault in the inverter/converter assembly (Toyota Highlander Hybrid)
Generator phase V current sensor failed
Poor pin fit or damaged three-phase cable to the generator

symptoms: MIL and master warning, several hybrid codes at once
Vehicle may not move or enter ready mode

P0A73.title: Generator Phase V Current Low
P0A73.description: P0A73 indicates that phase V of the hybrid generator delivers or reports too little current under load. No manufacturer documents P0A73 publicly. On inverters that measure only phases V and W, a low V reading has a knock-on effect: the calculated U current is wrong as well, so the generator torque control loses accuracy. A Caterpillar patent shows the logic for three-sensor systems, where a near-zero reading plus a violated zero-sum identifies the failed sensor; a Toyota patent compares a control sensor with a monitoring sensor and the current command. CARB requires circuit monitoring of electric drive components. P0A74 is the high side, P0A70 and P0A76 phases U and W, P0A72 the general code. Charging and engine start can suffer.

causes.label: Generator phase V current sensor reading near zero
Generator phase V lead or terminal open
Phase V switch in the generator inverter not conducting

symptoms: Hybrid warning and MIL
Engine runs more often, battery charge does not recover

P0A74.title: Generator Phase V Current High
P0A74.description: P0A74 appears when phase V of the hybrid generator shows more current than its limit allows. No manufacturer documents P0A74 publicly. A drifting sensor zero point is one candidate: a Hyundai patent covering both the traction motor and the starter-generator corrects phase sensor offsets and flags a fault when the correction fails. Real overcurrent is the other, for example from a winding or insulation short or a power switch that no longer turns off; a Toyota patent explains why the inverter then shuts down quickly. CARB requires monitoring of electric drive components. P0A73 is the low side, P0A71 and P0A77 phases U and W, P0A72 the general code. The hybrid system typically stops, and in power-split hybrids the car may lose drive entirely.

causes.label: Phase V sensor offset drifted or offset correction failed
Power switch in the generator phase V leg not turning off
Winding or insulation short in generator phase V

symptoms: Master warning or hybrid warning with MIL
Hybrid system shutdown, possibly no propulsion

P0A75.title: Generator Phase W Current
P0A75.description: P0A75 stands for a fault in the phase W current of the hybrid generator. Toyota documents it in practice: in a field report from an NHTSA investigation of 2006 Highlander Hybrid inverters, P0A75 appeared next to P0A72, the drive motor phase codes P0A60 and P0A63 and inverter performance codes, and the root cause was inside the inverter/converter, which was replaced. A sudden cluster like this points more to the shared inverter than to the generator winding. A Toyota patent shows how a control and a monitoring current sensor are cross-checked so that a defective sensor is caught before it causes overcurrent. P0A76 and P0A77 are the low and high variants, P0A6F and P0A72 phases U and V. Ready mode or drive may be lost.

causes.label: Internal fault in the inverter/converter assembly (Toyota Highlander Hybrid)
Generator phase W current sensor failed
Generator phase W cable or connector faulty

symptoms: MIL and master warning, usually with other hybrid codes
Vehicle will not become ready or will not move

P0A76.title: Generator Phase W Current Low
P0A76.description: P0A76 signals that phase W of the hybrid generator conducts or reports too little current while the generator should be producing or absorbing torque. No manufacturer documents P0A76 publicly. Physically, the generator phase leads run from the inverter into the transaxle or engine bay, so a loose bolted terminal, a cracked lead or a corroded connector can open the W path; electrically, a sensor fixed near zero gives the same reading. A Caterpillar patent separates both: a sensor fault is assumed when one phase reads about zero while the sum of the three no longer balances. A Hyundai patent shows separate generator phase sensors in the inverter. CARB requires circuit monitoring. P0A77 is the high side, P0A70 and P0A73 phases U and V.

causes.label: Loose terminal, cracked lead or corroded connector in generator phase W
Generator phase W current sensor stuck near zero
Open phase W winding in the generator

symptoms: Hybrid warning and MIL
Engine start harsh or delayed, charging reduced

P0A77.title: Generator Phase W Current High
P0A77.description: P0A77 is the excess-current code for phase W of the hybrid generator. No manufacturer documents P0A77 publicly. When the engine drives the generator hard, for instance while charging or during engine start, a short between turns, a breakdown to the housing or a switch that fails closed can let the W current climb beyond its limit; a sensor with too much gain produces a similar picture without real overcurrent. A Toyota patent, whose machine also works as generator, describes stopping the inverter and opening the relays when current runs away; a Caterpillar patent checks the zero-sum of the phase currents to unmask a bad sensor. CARB requires monitoring of electric drive components. P0A76 is the low side, P0A71 and P0A74 phases U and V.

causes.label: Turn-to-turn short or insulation breakdown in generator phase W
Power switch in the generator phase W leg failed closed
Generator phase W current sensor with excessive gain

symptoms: Master warning or hybrid warning with MIL
Hybrid system shuts down during charging or engine start

P0A78.title: Drive Motor A Inverter Performance
P0A78.description: P0A78 means the inverter stage feeding drive motor A has reported a power-switch fault. GM explains the check in its hybrid OBD tables: the IGBT module watches each phase for desaturation, a sign of a short between the upper and lower switch; if that status persists for about 2 ms the code sets as Type A, MIL on the first trip. Stellantis replaced the power inverter module on 2021 Jeep Wrangler 4xe with P0A78 and P0A79, which ran on engine power only, and refreshed hybrid control software on the 2017 Pacifica Hybrid. Land Rover logs P0A78 in the inverter converter of 2024-25 Range Rover models and asks not to clear it before diagnosis. P0A79 is motor B, P0A7A the generator inverter, P0A3C overheating of inverter A. Expect a warning and loss of electric drive.

causes.label: IGBT desaturation or short in the inverter power stage
Power inverter module defective (replaced on Jeep Wrangler 4xe)
Hybrid control software requiring update
Shorted winding or phase cable of drive motor A

symptoms: MIL and hybrid or high-voltage warning
No electric drive, engine-only operation
Stop safely warning on some models

P0A79.title: Drive Motor B Inverter Performance
P0A79.description: P0A79 is the drive motor B counterpart of P0A78: the inverter stage for motor B has detected a power-switch fault. In GM hybrid OBD tables the IGBT module reports a desaturation status on a high or low side switch of any phase; persisting for about 2 ms it sets P0A79 as Type A with MIL on the first trip. Stellantis documents P0A79 several times: on the 2021 Jeep Wrangler 4xe together with P0A78 and an engine-only limp mode, fixed by a new power inverter module; on the 2017 Pacifica Hybrid with improved hybrid control software, and with a loose high-voltage cable at the inverter terminal that also caused loss of propulsion. P0A78 is motor A, P0A7A the generator inverter, P0A3D overheating of inverter B. The driver loses electric drive.

causes.label: IGBT desaturation or short in the motor B power stage
Power inverter module defective
Loose high-voltage cable at the inverter terminal (Pacifica Hybrid)
Hybrid control software requiring update

symptoms: MIL and hybrid system warning
No electric drive, engine-only operation
Loss of propulsion in severe cases

P0A7A.title: Generator Inverter Performance
P0A7A.description: P0A7A reports that the inverter stage driving the generator has signalled a fault, for example overcurrent or a failed power switch. Toyota uses the code across its hybrids and splits it with information codes. Bulletin T-SB-0142-16 covers 2012-2016 Avalon, Camry and RAV4 Hybrid with MIL on and P0A7A plus information code 122, a generator inverter fail signal caused by overcurrent; the repair replaces inverter and transaxle. A Toyota field report filed with NHTSA describes a 2006 Highlander Hybrid with P0A7A sub code 325, master warning, MIL and Check Hybrid System, traced to a fault inside the inverter assembly. P0A78 and P0A79 are the drive motor inverters, P0A3E generator inverter overheating, P0A92 generator performance.

causes.label: Internal generator inverter fault with overcurrent (Toyota information code 122)
Inverter assembly defective
Fault in the generator inside the transaxle
Insufficient inverter cooling stressing the power stage

symptoms: MIL, master warning and Check Hybrid System message
Reduced power or vehicle will not enter ready mode

P0A7B.title: Battery Energy Control Module Requested MIL Illumination
P0A7B.description: P0A7B is a request code: the battery energy control module, which has found an emissions-relevant fault of its own, asks the engine control module to switch on the MIL, and the engine controller stores P0A7B. The actual cause sits in a separate code in the battery module. GM documents this on the 2024-25 Corvette E-Ray: P0A7B in the K20 engine controller appears together with P0E3C in the battery module, caused by air trapped around the battery coolant pump after a repair; purging the air is the fix. Subaru reports P0A7B in the engine controller of the 2014 XV Crosstrek Hybrid alongside battery and drive motor codes after a frozen power relay. Diagnose the battery module codes first. P0AC4 is the matching request from the hybrid control module.

causes.label: Emissions-relevant fault stored in the battery energy control module
Air trapped at the battery coolant pump (Corvette E-Ray, with P0E3C)
Frozen power supply relay of the drive motor control module (Subaru Crosstrek Hybrid)

symptoms: MIL on
Additional codes stored in the battery control module

P0A7C.title: Motor Electronics Over Temperature
P0A7C.description: P0A7C reports that the electronics controlling the hybrid motors, mainly the inverter, have run hotter than allowed. Ford uses the code on its hybrids and stores it in the PCM. A Ford bulletin for 2010-11 Fusion and Milan Hybrid and 2011 MKZ Hybrid built up to 9 September 2010 describes a wrench light with no drivability concern and P0A7C, cured by a PCM software update. Ford warranty statistics supplied to NHTSA list P0A7C as a recurring code on 2010-12 Escape, Tribute and Mariner Hybrid. Common physical causes are a failed coolant pump of the motor electronics cooling loop, low coolant, air in the loop or a blocked radiator. CARB requires monitoring of inverter thermal management. P0A3C and P0A3D cover the individual inverters. Power is reduced to protect the electronics.

causes.label: Coolant pump of the motor electronics cooling loop failed
Low coolant or air in the electronics cooling loop
PCM calibration triggering the code without real overheating (Ford Fusion Hybrid)
Blocked electronics radiator or faulty cooling fan

symptoms: Wrench or hybrid warning light
Reduced power, especially under high load or heat

P0A7D.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack State of Charge Low
P0A7D.description: The battery controller watches whether the traction or mild-hybrid pack stays inside its usable state-of-charge (SOC) window. GM sets P0A7D (Type B, two trips) when SOC stays below a program threshold (30 % or 10.5 %) for more than half of a drive cycle longer than 50 km, after allowing generator time to recover. Ford reports it on 2020 Escape/Explorer Hybrid after a deep discharge from long standing or crank/no-start, and Audi on 48 V systems whose protection relays open at low SOC. Unlike P0A7F/P0A80 the pack itself is not judged worn; it is simply too empty. Expect no EV mode, weak assist or, in severe cases, a no-start until the pack is recharged.

causes.label: Pack discharged by long standing time or repeated crank/no-start attempts
Generator, DC/DC or charging path not replenishing the pack
48 V battery in low-voltage protection state (relays open)
Weak or self-discharging cell modules

symptoms: Hybrid system or check engine warning
No electric driving or reduced motor assist
Engine runs longer to recharge the pack
Vehicle may not start or reach ready mode

P0A7E.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Over Temperature
P0A7E.description: The pack controller compares the hottest module temperature with a protection limit. GM sets P0A7E, mostly as Type A (MIL after one trip), when the maximum module temperature exceeds a program limit between about 61 and 73.5 °C, unless a temperature sensor fault is active. Subaru documents it on the 2014–16 Crosstrek Hybrid, where too strict logic for heat after shutdown cut assist and auto start-stop; GM links it on eAssist cars to a cooling fan that stops at low system voltage; Porsche saw it with implausible sensor signals on the 911 GTS T-Hybrid. Sensor circuit faults have their own codes (P0A9B–P0A9E). The car limits charge and discharge power to protect the cells.

causes.label: Battery cooling fan inoperative or intake/filter clogged
Battery controller software logic (update released by Subaru, Porsche)
Low 12 V system voltage stopping the cooling fan
Aged cells with high internal resistance heating up

symptoms: Hybrid system warning and check engine light
Reduced electric assist and regeneration
Auto start-stop no longer works
In rare cases warning with no-start

P0A7F.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Deterioration
P0A7F.description: This is the state-of-health monitor that CARB requires for hybrid storage systems. GM compares the calculated pack power capability with an end-of-life table at mid state of charge and sets P0A7F as Type B (two trips) when it falls short. Honda reports it as battery module deterioration on the 2009 Civic Hybrid and as serious capacity deterioration on the 2014 Accord Plug-In; Mercedes uses it when the 48 V module reaches its health limit, partly fixed by software. Toyota bulletins for Prius, Prius v and Camry Hybrid name a clogged battery cooling fan as a trigger. P0A80 is the harder replace-pack verdict. Drivers notice weaker assist, more engine running and higher fuel use.

causes.label: Pack capacity or power capability lost through ageing
Dust or debris in the battery cooling fan or filter overheating cells
Battery controller software misjudging health (Honda, Mercedes)
Individual weak modules pulling the pack down

symptoms: Check engine or hybrid/IMA warning light
Weak acceleration assist, especially from a stop
Engine runs more often, higher fuel consumption
Shorter electric range on plug-in models

P0A80.title: Replace Hybrid/EV Battery Pack
P0A80.description: The battery controller has concluded that the pack is at end of life. In GM tables this is a resistance test: the maximum cell or pack resistance, measured from current and voltage swings, exceeds a temperature-dependent end-of-life threshold, and the code sets as Type A after one trip. Toyota bulletins for Prius (2004–09, 2013–15), Prius v and Camry Hybrid report P0A80, often together with P0A7F, caused by dust in the battery cooling fan; cleaning the fan comes first. Honda recalled the 2018 Accord Hybrid because software wrongly set this code as a permanent fault after pack replacement. Compared with P0A7F it is the final verdict; assist and economy drop and the MIL stays on.

causes.label: Cell or module resistance above end-of-life limit
Clogged battery cooling fan or intake filter (Toyota)
Controller software misreading a replaced pack (Honda Accord Hybrid 2018)

symptoms: Check engine and hybrid system warning on
Noticeably weaker electric assist
Higher fuel consumption, engine runs more

P0A81.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Cooling Fan 1 Control Circuit/Open
P0A81.description: The controller watches the output that drives battery cooling fan 1 for an open circuit. In the 2016 GM table the fan is commanded at low duty (under 10 %) and the circuit voltage sits between about 1.6 and 5.85 V instead of being pulled low; 16 failures in 20 samples set it as Type B. An older GM program used it as a general fan unit fault judged by a monitor voltage. Ford found P0A81, often with P0A96 for fan 2, in the battery control module of 2005–12 Escape and Mariner Hybrids and replaced both fans; drivers usually noticed nothing. Low and high faults have their own codes (P0A84, P0A85). Without airflow the pack heats up and power may be limited.

causes.label: Fan motor or its internal electronics open
Loose or corroded fan connector, broken control wire
Blown fan supply fuse
Faulty output stage in the battery control module

symptoms: Check engine or hybrid warning, often no other complaint
Battery cooling fan does not run when commanded
Reduced hybrid power in hot conditions

P0A82.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Cooling Fan 1 Performance/Stuck Off
P0A82.description: This code covers a fan 1 that is electrically intact but does not deliver the requested cooling, up to standing still. No manufacturer publishes code-exact criteria; CARB requires a functional check of battery cooling where feasible. Typical methods: GM compares commanded and fed-back fan speed (filed under its own sense code P0BC8), Toyota flags a fan whose feedback-corrected duty deviates too far from the expected value, and Honda compares expected and measured battery temperature rise. Causes are mostly mechanical: dust on the blades, a clogged intake filter, worn bearings. Circuit faults use P0A81/P0A84/P0A85; the stuck-on case is P0A83. The pack runs hotter and power may be limited.

causes.label: Dust or debris on fan blades or in the duct
Clogged or covered battery air intake or filter
Worn or seized fan motor bearings
Faulty fan speed feedback signal

symptoms: Hybrid warning or check engine light
Fan audibly weak or silent under load
Reduced electric assist in warm weather

P0A83.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Cooling Fan 1 Stuck On
P0A83.description: P0A83 means battery cooling fan 1 keeps turning although the controller has switched it off. No manufacturer publicly documents this exact code. CARB asks for fan outputs to be checked for proper response to commands. GM shows the method under its sense code P0BC8: with the fan off for more than 20 s, a reported speed above 120 rpm counts as a fault. Likely causes are a control wire shorted to supply, a welded fan relay (GM files that as P0BC1) or a fan controller that ignores the command. The pack stays cool, but the fan drains the 12 V battery when parked and stays loud. Do not confuse it with P0A82 (fan too weak or off) or the circuit codes P0A81/P0A84/P0A85.

causes.label: Fan control wire shorted to supply voltage
Welded fan relay keeps power applied
Fan's internal speed controller ignores off command
Battery control module output stuck active

symptoms: Battery fan heard running with the vehicle off or idle
Discharged 12 V battery after parking
Hybrid or check engine warning

P0A84.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Cooling Fan 1 Control Circuit Low
P0A84.description: The controller detects a short to ground on the control output of battery cooling fan 1. GM tests it while the fan is commanded at low duty: a circuit voltage below about 0.26 V counts as a failure, and 16 fails in 20 samples at 250 ms set a Type B code (MIL after two trips). Another GM hybrid program detects it through the output stage status flag (20 of 25 samples). Mitsubishi lists P0A84 in the BMU and PHEV ECU of the 2018–20 Outlander PHEV among codes caused by a frozen battery heater relay, so meaning can differ by maker. Open and high faults are P0A81 and P0A85. With the output pulled low the fan may not respond, the pack warms up and power can be reduced.

causes.label: Fan control wire chafed and shorted to ground
Internal short in the fan's control input
Moisture or corrosion in the fan connector
Defective output stage in the controller

symptoms: Check engine or hybrid warning after two trips
Battery cooling fan does not follow commands
Reduced hybrid power when the pack gets warm

P0A85.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Cooling Fan 1 Control Circuit High
P0A85.description: The controller detects a short to voltage on the control output of battery cooling fan 1. GM runs the test while the fan is commanded between 11 % and 100 % duty: a circuit voltage above 9 V counts as a failure, and 16 fails in 20 samples set a Type B code with MIL after two trips. GM tables from 2013, 2016, 2018 and 2019 hybrid programs carry it, partly via the output stage status flag. Depending on the circuit, the fan may run constantly at full speed or not respond. The low and open counterparts are P0A84 and P0A81; a fan that keeps running without a circuit fault is P0A83.

causes.label: Control wire shorted to a supply voltage
Fan control input internally open or shorted to its supply
Corroded connector creating leakage to supply

symptoms: Check engine or hybrid warning after two trips
Battery fan runs constantly or not at all
Possible 12 V battery drain when parked

P0A86.title: 14 Volt Power Module Current Sensor A Circuit
P0A86.description: The 14 volt power module is the DC/DC converter that feeds the 12 V network of a hybrid or electric vehicle from the high-voltage battery; GM calls it the Accessory Power Module (APM). Current sensor A measures the current flowing through this converter. P0A86 is the general circuit code for that sensor, used when the controller recognises a fault in the sensor circuit without classifying it as low, high, implausible or intermittent (P0A87 to P0A8A). No manufacturer documents this code publicly; GM's published tables for the same APM input sensor use only the low/high codes P0A88 and P0A89. With an untrustworthy current reading the hybrid controller may limit or switch off the converter, so the 12 V battery can run down over time.

causes.label: Current sensor inside the 14 V power module faulty (usually not replaceable separately)
Damaged wiring or corroded connector between module and hybrid controller
Software fault in the module or hybrid controller

symptoms: Hybrid or charging system warning lamp on
12 V battery discharges, low-voltage warnings
Possibly no other noticeable change in driving

P0A87.title: 14 Volt Power Module Current Sensor A Circuit Range/Performance
P0A87.description: This code means the current sensor of the 14 V power module (DC/DC converter, GM: APM) delivers values that are electrically valid but implausible. GM's 2016 eAssist tables (hybrid control processor HPC1) describe a stuck-in-range test: once per key cycle, while the high-voltage contactors are open and then move to precharge, the converter should be off, so the averaged input current must be near zero. If the average is 0.50 A or more, P0A87 sets as a Type B code, so the MIL comes on after two failed trips. The test is skipped while P0A88 or P0A89 is active. Unlike those circuit low/high codes, the wiring is usually intact here; a sensor with offset drift is the typical finding.

causes.label: Current sensor zero-point drift inside the power module
Converter actually conducting current when it should be off (internal module fault)
Ground or reference fault distorting the sensor signal

symptoms: MIL on after two drive cycles
Usually no driveability change
Possible reduced 12 V charging if the converter is limited

P0A88.title: 14 Volt Power Module Current Sensor A Circuit Low
P0A88.description: P0A88 reports that the current sensor of the 14 V power module (DC/DC converter feeding the 12 V system) reads too low while the converter should be delivering power. GM documents it for the Accessory Power Module: in the 2013 eAssist tables the input current must stay below 0.5 A for 1.5 s within a 2 s window while calculated output power is 0.25 to 1.5 kW; the 2016 tables use 0.50 A or less in 640 of 800 samples, enabled only when the APM is on, the hood is closed and the 12 V target is reached. Both rate it Type B, two trips to MIL. A short to ground, an open signal line or a dead sensor are typical; P0A89 is the opposite high fault, P0A87 the plausibility check.

causes.label: Sensor signal shorted to ground or open
Current sensor in the power module failed
Corroded or loose module connector

symptoms: MIL and hybrid/charging warning
12 V battery not charged properly
Start/stop function may be disabled

P0A89.title: 14 Volt Power Module Current Sensor A Circuit High
P0A89.description: P0A89 is set when the current sensor of the 14 V power module reports more current than the converter can physically carry. GM's eAssist tables show how: in 2013 the APM input current reading had to exceed 22.5 A for 1.5 s while calculated output power was 1.5 kW or less; in 2016 the limit is 45.25 A or more in 200 of 250 samples (about 5 s) with the APM commanded on and 9 to 32 V supply. Both versions classify it Type B, so the MIL lights after the second failing trip. Typical causes are a signal short to voltage or an internal sensor fault. P0A88 is the low counterpart, P0A87 the in-range plausibility test, and the APM output sensor has its own codes (P0C9E/P0C9F).

causes.label: Sensor signal shorted to supply voltage
Current sensor in the power module failed
Open sensor ground pulling the signal high

symptoms: MIL and hybrid/charging warning
Converter output limited, 12 V voltage drops
Start/stop function may be disabled

P0A8A.title: 14 Volt Power Module Current Sensor A Circuit Intermittent
P0A8A.description: P0A8A covers short dropouts or jumps in the signal of the current sensor in the 14 V power module, the DC/DC converter that charges the 12 V battery in hybrids and EVs. The signal is valid most of the time but briefly leaves its range or changes faster than physically possible. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; GM's APM tables only show the hard limits for the same sensor (P0A88 below 0.5 A, P0A89 above 22.5 A or 45.25 A), which indicates what the intermittent check guards against. Loose terminals, chafed wiring near the module and vibration are the usual suspects. Compared with P0A88/P0A89 the fault often clears and returns, which makes freeze-frame data valuable.

causes.label: Loose or fretted terminals at the module connector
Chafed wiring with intermittent short or open
Intermittent internal fault of the current sensor

symptoms: Warning lamp that comes and goes
Occasional 12 V voltage fluctuations

P0A8B.title: 14 Volt Power Module System Voltage
P0A8B.description: The 14 V power module (DC/DC converter) regulates the voltage of the 12 V network in hybrid and electric vehicles. P0A8B is the general code for a fault in the voltage this module produces or senses, without the more specific labels unstable, low, high or performance (P0A8C to P0A8F). No manufacturer documents this code publicly. GM's 2013 eAssist tables show how the sibling codes are used for the same function: the APM low-voltage sensor is checked against fixed limits and against the separately measured run/crank voltage. A fault here means the 12 V system may no longer be supplied reliably, so the 12 V battery and consumers should be checked before the module is condemned.

causes.label: Internal fault of the DC/DC converter
Loose or corroded 12 V output cable or ground connection
Weak 12 V battery distorting the system voltage

symptoms: Charging or hybrid system warning
Electrical consumers behave erratically
12 V battery discharged

P0A8C.title: 14 Volt Power Module System Voltage Unstable
P0A8C.description: P0A8C indicates that the output voltage of the 14 V power module, the DC/DC converter supplying the 12 V network of a hybrid or EV, fluctuates beyond what the control strategy accepts instead of settling at its target. Possible reasons include a poor 12 V connection, an aged 12 V battery that no longer buffers the network, or a regulation problem inside the converter. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; GM's APM tables only cover low, high and performance faults of the same voltage (P0A8D, P0A8E, P0A8F). For the driver, flickering lights, resets of electronic units or start/stop being disabled are typical. Unlike P0A8D/P0A8E the average voltage may still be normal.

causes.label: Loose or corroded 12 V battery terminal or ground strap
Aged 12 V battery no longer buffering the network
Unstable regulation inside the DC/DC converter

symptoms: Flickering lights or display resets
Charging or hybrid system warning
Start/stop disabled

P0A8D.title: 14 Volt Power Module System Voltage Low
P0A8D.description: P0A8D reports too low a voltage at the 14 V power module (DC/DC converter feeding the 12 V network). GM uses it in its 2013 eAssist tables as the circuit-low check of the APM low-voltage sensor: if that sensor reads below 1 V for 1.5 s within a 2 s window while ignition voltage is 9 to 32 V, the code sets; it passes again above 1.5 V. It is Type B, two trips to MIL. Because a real 12 V network cannot be at 1 V with the ignition on, GM's version really points to an open or shorted voltage sense line or a failed sensor, not a flat battery. Other makers may apply the code to genuine undervoltage. P0A8E is the high counterpart, P0A8F the correlation check.

causes.label: Voltage sense line open or shorted to ground
Voltage sensor inside the power module failed
Converter not delivering output (fuse, output cable)

symptoms: MIL and charging/hybrid warning
12 V battery discharges
Start/stop disabled

P0A8E.title: 14 Volt Power Module System Voltage High
P0A8E.description: P0A8E signals too high a voltage at the 14 V power module, the DC/DC converter supplying the 12 V side. In GM's 2013 eAssist tables it is the circuit-high check of the APM low-voltage sensor: a reading above 20 V for 1.5 s within a 2 s window, with ignition voltage 9 to 32 V, sets the code, and it passes below 19.5 V. GM rates it Type B, so the MIL comes on after two failing trips. Since the network should sit around 14 V, a reading over 20 V usually means a sense line shorted to a higher potential or a faulty sensor; a genuinely over-regulating converter would also threaten bulbs and modules. P0A8D is the low counterpart, P0A8F compares the sensor with the ignition voltage.

causes.label: Voltage sense line shorted to a higher potential
Voltage sensor inside the power module failed
Converter regulating its output too high

symptoms: MIL and charging/hybrid warning
Very bright lights or failing bulbs if overvoltage is real
Converter may be shut down

P0A8F.title: 14 Volt Power Module System Performance
